text:
tess_devex: Quick note — found a quirky UX around the ruby SDK and streaming when tokens rotate. Sample app drops the stream; go client keeps going.

omar_rb: thanks, can you share steps?

tess_devex: repro: start streaming demo, trigger token rotation from admin endpoint, ruby client raises EOFError and stops. gist: https://gist.github.com/example-repro

nina_sre: sounds like our http lib closes on 401 mid-stream. go has transport-level retry behavior we don't mirror.

omar_rb: current code basically does `while chunk = socket.readpartial(4096)
  yield chunk
end` and lets EOF bubble. We should reconnect + re-auth on EOF/ECONNRESET and continue.

pat_support: customers in a training hit this; they restart the quickstart which is annoying.

tess_devex: i've opened a tiny PR that rescues EOFError and Errno::ECONNRESET, calls `auth.refresh_if_needed`, reconnects with exponential backoff, and continues the stream. Added a unit test for mid-stream rotation. PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/2522

ci-bot: PR 2522 — CI: linux/x86_64 passed, linux/arm64 passed, macos failed (bundle install mismatch), windows pending.

omar_rb: macOS bundler mismatch again. We should avoid touching Gemfile.lock in this fix. Nina, can CI pin bundler version instead?

nina_sre: yes, i'll pin bundler in the macOS job to 2.3.5 so it's consistent with the lockfile.

pat_support: can we add a short README note in the sampleapp about token rotation behaviour and the new client handling? Saves support tickets.

tess_devex: will add docs + changelog entry. After nina's CI pin and green windows I'll merge. Also adding a small integration test that runs the sampleapp and performs a rotation to assert reconnect.

omar_rb: when reconnecting, be careful about partial JSON events — buffer until a newline or full object before yielding.

tess_devex: yes — implemented a small buffer and tests for partial-chunk reassembly. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

ci-bot: windows CI finished: passed. macOS pinned bundler job re-run: passed. All checks green.
